I farm 20 mu under a wheat-maize rotation, so I will put the full 20 mu into winter wheat first and then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. Because my family has some off-farm work, I will keep the plan practical and not too labor-heavy. I have well irrigation, so I will use it to protect yield instead of gambling on rainfall. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate-high fertilizer, and a few irrigations because wheat in my area responds well to water and nitrogen. I will use rotary tillage after maize harvest because it is simpler and faster for me than deep ploughing every year. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me better yield potential on irrigated land. I will keep fertilizer balanced, irrigate when key growth stages need it, and control pests with limited but timely sprays. I will aim for stable output more than extreme input use, because with 20 mu and some labor constraints, I want dependable yields and manageable costs.
